issues.what: The reverse image search returned R1 Reuters 'israelis-rally-again-against-governments-judicial-overhaul-2023-03-04' with image=ready(E8), plus R4 Malay Mail (E12) and R5 Asharq Al-Awsat (E10), all with fetched images. None of them was ever compared with E1 and R1 never got a date lookup. Only R2 and R7 were compared. The report and the FINISH then say 'The first publisher and publication date of the exact photograph could not be determined'.
issues.why_bad_to_teach: It teaches the student to skip the candidate that matters most: a major-agency copy whose URL date is before the claim date and whose image was already fetched, and then to call provenance undeterminable.
issues.ideal: Run compare_media on E1 against E8 (Reuters 2023-03-04) and E12/E10, and do a date lookup on R1, before reporting INCOMPLETE.

issues.what: The round-2 task sends the worker to France 24, Mother Jones and JPost. Those are hits from the generic text search, not the reverse-image hits. The task only says 'open and read' each page: it has no 'first fetch the main image ... and compare it' item. It also carries the premise 'Verify if the image depicts protests in Israel'. The uncompared reverse-image hits (R1 Reuters E8, R4 E12, R5 E10) are left out.
issues.why_bad_to_teach: It teaches a follow-up plan that chases loosely related text pages instead of the visual matches already found, and it frames a hypothesis as the thing to verify.
issues.ideal: Round 2 should first compare E1 with the already-fetched reverse-image candidates (E8, E12, E10) and date R1. Any gallery page assigned should come with an explicit step to fetch its image and compare.

issues.what: The worker opens and reads the text of three photo-gallery pages but never fetches or compares any of their images. The report then admits 'The article's photographs were not compared with the given image' and comes back INCOMPLETE with only topic-level findings (F3-F5 just restate article text).
issues.why_bad_to_teach: On an image-provenance task, reading only the text of photo galleries cannot establish a match. Imitating this round produces six turns that add nothing to the verdict.
issues.ideal: For each gallery page, fetch the main image(s) and run compare_media against E1 before summarising the caption.

issues.what: OCR had just returned '0 text boxes ... no text was recognised', yet the rationales assert banner text. Turn 2 says "banners reading 'RESIST' and 'YOGI STARTUP NATION'". Turn 3 says "'FROM STARTUP NATION TO SHUTDOWN NATION' and 'MUST RESIST'". Later turns say "'RESIST' and Hebrew text". The readings disagree with each other and are used to declare that E1 'contradicts the claim'. Neither worker report ever mentions any legible banner text (W2-1 F1 says only 'banners suspended above the crowd').
issues.why_bad_to_teach: The student learns to make up specific sign text, inconsistent from turn to turn and contradicted by the OCR tool, and to reach a verdict from it before any matching.
issues.ideal: Describe only what OCR or a visible zoom confirms (e.g. 'OCR found no text; banners are visible but unreadable'). If the text matters, zoom on the banners or OCR a crop.

issues.what: The rationale says 'Reverse image search identified R7 (WION) as a matching source for E1', but the observation says 'Thumbnail compared with the query image: no match', and compare_media later shows 50.31% changed area.
issues.why_bad_to_teach: It teaches the student to treat any search hit as a match, which feeds attribution drift.
issues.ideal: Call R7 'a candidate returned by Google Lens (thumbnail did not hash-match)' and check its dates as a candidate.

issues.what: The text query 'aerial night protest crowd banners Hebrew Israel judicial reform 2023' is generic and builds in the unverified Israel hypothesis. It returns topic galleries (Wikipedia, Getty, Mother Jones), not copies of E1.
issues.why_bad_to_teach: It teaches a confirmation-style topic search in place of the provenance work that was still open (uncompared image hits).
issues.ideal: Compare the already-fetched reverse-image candidates first. If a text search is needed, use distinctive verified features from the photo.

issues.what: The limitation states '3 of 7 candidate pages failed to load', but the search result shows page=failed for R1, R3, R4, R5 and R6, which is 5 of 7.
issues.why_bad_to_teach: Miscounting tool failures understates how much of the negative result comes from tool failure.
issues.ideal: '5 of 7 candidate pages failed to load (R1, R3-R6); their images E8, E12, E10 were fetched but not compared.'

issues.what: The answer ends with 'its location, capture date, event and relationship to the claim dated 26 March 2023 therefore remain undetermined'. It never says that every reverse-image hit (Reuters, WION, Malay Mail, Al-Monitor, etc.) concerned Israeli judicial-reform protests and none concerned France. It also leaves out that the image candidates were not all checked.
issues.why_bad_to_teach: It teaches the student to drop the consistent counter-context the evidence does show, and to present an incomplete investigation as an evidence ceiling.
issues.ideal: State that the reverse-image results point consistently to Israeli judicial-reform coverage (Feb-Jul 2023) with no French copies, mark it as unconfirmed pending a direct match, and name the uncompared candidates as the gap.

issues.what: The rationales keep opening with the same template, 'E1 shows an aerial night protest with banners reading 'RESIST' and Hebrew text, contradicting the claim...', almost word for word across steps whatever the action.
issues.why_bad_to_teach: Mechanical boilerplate teaches the student to repeat a stock opener instead of reasoning about the current step.
issues.ideal: Each rationale should state what the previous observation established and why this specific action follows.

good_patterns: The OCR result is reported honestly ('OCR can miss text, so this does not show there is none'), and the reports never use the archive date as the image date ('An archive capture establishes existence by that date, not first publication').

Candidates are compared with compare_media before their context is trusted, and the comparison composite (E24) is reviewed before reporting. The report calls Minanews a 'candidate' and refuses to give WION's 2023-02-26 date to the non-matching photo.
The final answer does not adopt the circulating claim and keeps candidate context separate from established context, citing evidence ids throughout.
Limitations on compare_media percentages are accurate ('The percentage alone does not distinguish changes in viewpoint, capture time, resizing, compression or editing').
cannot_judge: The actual content of E1, E5, E15 and the composites E21/E24: whether the banners are legible, whether they say what the rationales claim, and whether Minanews E5 is really the same scene with local edits or a different photo.
The truncated search results for R6-R10 (+1387 chars), which may hold match-type or date info for the Reuters/AP/Reddit hits.
The full text of E16, E26, E27 and E28 (truncated), including whether any of them captions an aerial night shot matching E1.
The contents of the date records E18/E19 beyond the one-line summaries.
summary: The run handles candidate wording and date semantics carefully, but its provenance work is shallow. W1-1 compares only two of the fetched reverse-image images and ignores a Reuters copy dated 2023-03-04 (E8) that was already retrieved. Round 2 then spends a whole workspace reading the text of three topic galleries without comparing any images. Throughout, the rationales assert banner text ('RESIST', 'YOGI STARTUP NATION', 'FROM STARTUP NATION TO SHUTDOWN NATION') that OCR did not find and that changes between turns. The final 'undetermined' answer is honest about what was established, but it partly reflects skipped steps rather than an evidence ceiling.
